title: Father, Breathe an Evening Blessing
description: Father, Breathe an Evening Blessing in Tonic Solfa to OMNI DIE, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: James Edmeston wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 942 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Confidence in God's Protection”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Eights and Sevens (8.7.8.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OMNI DIE; any other Eights and Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Fa-ther, breathe an eve-ning bless-ing Ere re-pose our spi-rits seal; Sin and want we come con-fes-sing; Thou canst save and thou canst heal.

lines: Sin and want we come confessing;
Thou canst save and thou canst heal.
Though the arrows past us fly,
Angel guards from thee surround us;
We are safe, if thou art nigh.
Though the night be dark and dreary,
Thou art he who, never weary,
Should swift death this night o'ertake us,
And command us to the tomb,
May the morn in heaven awake us,

licence: Public domain: James Edmeston died in 1867.
credits: Words by James Edmeston (1791–1867), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to OMNI DIE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
